classification.difficultyReason: Track the same two counts across interchanged denominations, form and scale two cost equations, solve and interpret the original allocation.

content.prompt:
Solve by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though the problem may be done more easily using one pronumeral.

A secretary buys a number of 45-cent and 60-cent stamps for a total cost of $\$22.50$. If he interchanges the numbers of the two kinds of stamps, the total cost would have been $\$23.70$. How many of each kind of stamp did he originally buy?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the original number of 45-cent stamps and $y$ the original number of 60-cent stamps. Express costs in cents.

$$\begin{align*}45x+60y&=2250 &&(1)\\60x+45y&=2370 &&(2)\\3x+4y&=150 &&(3)\\4x+3y&=158 &&(4)\end{align*}$$

Eliminate $y$ using $4\times(4)-3\times(3)$.

$$\begin{align*}16x+12y&=632\\9x+12y&=450\\7x&=182\\x&=26\end{align*}$$

Substitute $x=26$ into equation (3).

$$\begin{align*}3(26)+4y&=150\\78+4y&=150\\4y&=72\\y&=18\end{align*}$$

He originally bought 26 forty-five-cent stamps and 18 sixty-cent stamps.

Check: $45(26)+60(18)=2250$ cents, and $45(18)+60(26)=2370$ cents.
